calc_items.title: Pre/postductal saturation difference
calc_items.question: On CCHD pulse-oximetry screening, right-hand SpO₂ is 97% and foot SpO₂ is 92%. What is the absolute pre/postductal difference?
calc_items.working: Absolute difference = |97 − 92| = 5 percentage points. Under IAP-NNF 2026 this is indeterminate (unless either site is <90%): one rescreen after 1 hour.
calc_items.trap: Use the absolute difference, and read the screen category from the named protocol.

calc_items.title: Arm–leg systolic gradient
calc_items.question: Right-arm systolic BP is 74 mmHg and leg systolic BP is 48 mmHg. What is the arm–leg gradient?
calc_items.working: Gradient = 74 − 48 = 26 mmHg; a significant arch-obstruction clue in IAP-NNF 2026.
calc_items.trap: Compare the right arm (preductal) with a leg.

calc_items.title: Prostaglandin dose rate
calc_items.question: A 3.0-kg neonate needs prostaglandin E1 at 0.05 microgram/kg/min. What is the dose in microgram/min and in microgram/hour?
calc_items.trap: High-alert educational arithmetic only; use the local dilution and infusion protocol.

calc_items.title: Infusion pump rate
calc_items.question: An authorised 5 microgram/mL syringe is used to give a calculated 9 microgram/hour dose. What pump rate is needed?
calc_items.trap: Independently verify the concentration and pump set-up at the bedside.

calc_items.title: Ventricular rate from the R–R interval
calc_items.question: The R–R interval on a neonatal ECG is 0.40 s. What is the ventricular rate?
calc_items.trap: Classify the rate for age and context, not by adult cut-offs.
